title: BEST OF THE BEST!  HERE'S WHY...
body:
Having worn all of Beardbrand's EDPs, I've come to sort them into three categories: Good, Great, and EXCELLENT.vvAnd make no mistake, they're all good. But some fragrances simply stand a little taller than the rest.  In the Great category, you've got Old Money, Fox Hunt, and Four Vices. These are fragrances that make you take another breath, and appreciate what's happening
 Then there's the EXCELLENT category: Norse Winter and Faded Denim.  And of those two, Faded Denim is the undisputed champion. The crown jewel. The best of the best. 

 This fragrance is an absolute masterpiece of blending. The bright, sparkling bergamot opens the door like a burst of sunlight. A peppery spice adds just the right amount of warmth, while the leather brings a rugged sophistication that feels like a well-worn leather jacket that's somehow always in style. Vanilla softens the edges, sandalwood adds a creamy, polished warmth, and incense and agarwood provide a deep, mysterious, almost hypnotic foundation. 

 It's clean, but not sterile. Warm, not heavy. Sophisticated, not stuffy. Every note seems to know exactly where it belongs--a beautifully orchestrated composition where every instrument plays its part, and the result is olfactory magic. 

 Of every Beardbrand EDP, Faded Denim is, IMHO, far and away my favorite. It doesn't just raise the bar; it moves the entire bar to another building!  I fully intend to purchase more of this EDP. And PLEASE, Beardbrand, don't let this fragrance be a one-and-done offering!  MAKE THIS A FULL PRODUCT LINE!  It's SOOOO good!!

title: From the Fragrance Creator
body:
I love the American spirit and history of this great country. The people who have set out for new opportunities to build a better life. I think about my time as a kid playing the Oregon Trail and what those people went through. I think about the nature they passed through on their journey from St Louis to the west. 

 And then I think about their lives as they hit the mines, cut down the trees, or setup shop. 

 There is fewer things more Americana than denim and the story that can be told through a worn pair of denim. Something that collects blood, sweat, dirt and tears. 

 Worn Denim isn't a fragrance about denim, it's a fragrance of the story of settling the west, of seeking adventure and the notes found along the way.  

 Worn Denim smells like the dawn on the trail and the cold air with a bite of citrus from last night's provisions. The pepper and spices in the pot and the wild oregano crushed under the wheels on a dry hillside. 

 The leather notes will start to take over in the midday sun and then as that sun fades the smoke from the wood settles into place; slowly and deeply. A hint of vanilla, the last luxury remaining on their treacherous journey.  

 If you like Norse Winter or Old Money I think you're going to love this one. Enjoy!

title: From Asking for a Refund to My Favorite Scent
body:
When I first took a whiff of this scent, it immediately reminded me of a brown Levi’s leather jacket. I liked it, but I wasn’t entirely sure it was the kind of fragrance I was looking for. 

 Fast forward a week, and somehow it’s become my absolute favorite scent. I reach for it more than anything else I own, which is pretty funny considering I initially asked for a refund! 

 If there’s one thing I’ve learned, it’s to give a fragrance at least a week before making up your mind. It’s fascinating how your perception of a scent can change over time. 

 What I love most is how this fragrance evolves as you wear it. That initial leather note gradually softens, allowing all these other incredible layers to come through, notes I honestly can't even put into words. The more I wear it, the more I appreciate its complexity. 

 To think I almost gave up on it! Now, without question, it's my number one favorite scent.

title: Bold Fortune Cologne
body: I have already given a review of Four Vices cologne, and this is my review of Bold Fortune.  it has a very complex scent that ends with a fine tobacco finish. It  might become overwhelming if not used properly...which is sparingly.  I find it to be a mysterious blend that instantly captures the interest of others...warm, rich and aromatic.  Just remember that a dab will do ya, and you can't go wrong!

It really is true that it smells like nothing else that I own/have owned. It is a close skin scent after about 30 minutes, perfect for cuddling or close encounters. it seems to last about 5ish hour with pretty good silage for the 1st hour. The smell is a woodsy, darker scent with some refined freshness that smells clean. It is a very manly smell, hints of wood, gunpowder and a muted sweetness like vanilla, the same vibe as mixing Kilians Black Phantom with Tom Ford tobacco Vanille, but not nearly as nuclear. You will need to reapply if you wish the scent to carry all day, perfect to carry with you, pop in the glovebox or in a bag. It is a compliment magnet after hugs, standing close to others and holds a unique profile that you stand out from the trend of loud and sharp colognes/parfums going on right now. People remember this scent. Perfect as a signature scent.

title: A Scent With Some Soul
body:
I’ve been a Beardbrand guy for a while now, and Temple Smoke has been my go-to for almost a year. I absolutely love that scent—it has character, depth, and that slightly smoky, old-school vibe that I’m drawn to. 

 But Black Sails… damn. This one really grabbed me. 

 It’s dark, warm, woody, slightly smoky, and mysterious without being heavy or obnoxious. It has personality. It smells like something you’d discover in an old record store, a dimly lit bar, or some forgotten club where the music is actually good. There’s something vintage about it, but it doesn’t smell dated. It just smells cool. 

 I’m pretty particular about fragrances. I don’t want to smell like every other guy wearing the latest department-store cologne. I want something with a little soul to it, and Black Sails absolutely delivers. 

 Temple Smoke will always have a place in the rotation, but Black Sails has quickly become a favorite. It’s one of those scents that feels less like “putting on cologne” and more like putting the finishing touch on the whole vibe. 

 Seriously good stuff! Bravo Beard Brand!

title: Cologne’s I Love
body:
For the last 20 years, I have worn only one cologne. That cologne is “1903”, by the Jpeterman company, until I saw the commercial about “Black Sails” by BeardBrand. It appealed to me because I love novels about tall sailing ships, and even retired out of the Navy. A cologne with gunpowder in it? So I purchased it and fell in love with it. Then I purchased a small bottle of “Norse Winter”. When I put it on, and closed my eyes, I felt like I was sitting in a log cabin in front of a roaring fire and surrounded by pine trees outside, and drinking a fine aged bourbon.It was wonderful. I began putting a little dab on each wrist every night, before I went to bed. It helped me to relax, and fall asleep.
 I knew then, that I had to explore all of the other fragrances from BeardBrand. I have been on a wonderful journey ever since.
 Thank you, BeardBrand, for bringing something new and exciting into my life.

title: The only one that I will buy, here is why.
body: Old Money cologne used to be amazing in the old spray formula. In roller, it is the same, also amazing. It is rich, complex, has projection and lasting power. Sadly, it is THE ONLY Beardbrand cologne that has these traits. The others fade within 10 minutes, no one can smell them (even if applying quadruple the recommended amount) and are not "colognes". These are just oil with scent and the scent doesn't really stick. I have spent a couple hundred here on these and only one is worth the cost. I feel the others should be dropped personally as they do nothing really, just for a few minutes. Temple Smoke lasts 7 minutes with zero projection. Same with Norse Winter, Fox Hunt and Short Game. Desert Road is OK but still not like a cologne..dull, one noted and no projection. I will order more Old Money when I run out and I do have beard oil, balm, deodorant and cologne in Temple, Norse and Old but even Norse and Temple colognes are not worth it for me as again, they fade within minutes and I can't even smell them after that. They just are not anything like a real cologne let alone an EDP.  I still love the brand, just feel they miss more then they hit when it comes to colognes.

title: Can’t live without it
body: This is a necessary part of my leaving the house ritual. I live in a windy area and my beard seriously blossoms in the wind. I use beard oil and have used balm in the past  but the only thing that tames this monster is the Seal Salt Spray. I quickly shape it after spraying and then leave it alone for a couple minutes while it dries and then I am good to go. No more poodle face. My beard stays soft and it is not at all noticeable that I used the spray. It layers nicely with the Cologne and Beard Oil. The fragrance of Norse Winter slowly evolves on me as the day progresses and it has a very pleasing scent throughout the day. The taste however leaves much to be desired. I sometimes forget to keep my mouth closed when I hit my ‘stache and beard with the spray, but I am very quickly reminded of my lapse. On the rare occasion that I wear a suit and tie, this really helps keep the shape as the whole shirt collar and tie and jacket don’t play well with the lay of my beard. This is a really nice part of the collection and makes my life a bit simpler.

title: IN BEARDBRAND'S TOP THREE, FOR SURE!
body: This is the best, next to Norse Winter and Old Money.  Unique and comfortably classic.  Begins as a crisp scent (probably the lemon note) and evolves into a soft, spicy-woody scent.
